tagline: Prairie, crane country and the house where The Yearling was written.
intro: Just south of Gainesville the byway follows US 441 past Paynes Prairie and Micanopy toward McIntosh, with county roads looping off through Rochelle, Evinston and Cross Creek past small lakes, prairies and rural homesteads. Sandhill cranes winter along County Roads 325 and 346.

The River Styx Road to Micanopy, CR 346, was not paved until 1962. When Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings moved to Cross Creek in 1928 it was seven families on unpaved roads, with no electric power and no ice.

moments.title: Paynes Prairie
moments.text: Seen from the outlook on US 441 it is a savanna, but from 1871 to 1891 it was a lake with steamboats on it, until the water drained away in 1891 and marooned one.

moments.title: Micanopy
moments.text: The oldest continuously inhabited community in Florida's interior goes by the motto "The Town that Time Forgot" and keeps its antique stores in a downtown historic district.

moments.title: Marjorie Kinnan Rawlings Historic State Park
moments.text: The rambling cracker house where The Yearling was written stands on the east shore of Orange Lake among Rawlings' orange trees, and visitors are invited to pick one.
